name: Terpene combination (pinene, camphene, borneol, fenchone, anethole, cineole)
className: Terpene (essential oil) combination for urinary stones
searchTerms: pinene camphene borneol cineole fenchone anethole

formulations.label: Gastro-resistant soft capsules
formulations.strengths: Per capsule: pinene (alpha + beta) 31 mg, camphene 15 mg, cineole 3 mg, fenchone 4 mg, borneol 10 mg, anethole 4 mg
formulations.note: Capsule shell contains hydroxybenzoates (E215, E217), sunset yellow and glycerol.

src.q: Pinene [a + β] 31.0mg Camphene 15.0 mg Cineol BPC 3.0 mg Fenchone 4.0 mg Borneol 10.0 mg Anethol USP 4.0 mg
The capsules are gastro-resistant.
This medicine may cause allergic reactions (possibly delayed) as it contains sodium ethyl hydroxybenzoate (E215) and sodium propyl hydroxybenzoate (E217).

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

items.t: Urolithiasis and nephrolithiasis (helps stones break up and pass; relieves mild to moderate renal and urinary colic from stones); relief of frequency and urgency in mild urinary tract infection.

src.q: Urolithiasis, nephrolithiasis and mild urinary tract infections.
gives symptomatic relief of mild to moderate renal and urinary colic associated with the presence of stones in the renal and urinary tracts
is also indicated for the relief of frequency and urgency associated with mild urinary tract infections

items.t: Not suitable for severe colic, anuria or severe urinary tract infection. The UK SPC text dates from 2004.

src.q: is not suitable for use in patients with severe colic, anuria or severe infection of the urinary tract
DATE OF (PARTIAL) REVISION OF TEXT 29/06/2004

items.t: One capsule 3 or 4 times daily before meals (PIL: half an hour before meals).

src.q: Adults: One capsule 3 or 4 times daily before meals.
Take one capsule 3-4 times daily, half an hour before meals.

items.t: SPC: no dose recommendation for children. PIL: under 18 years should not take it.

src.q: No dose recommendation for children.
Children and adolescents under 18 years of age should not take Rowatinex®.

items.t: SPC 4.3: none known. PIL: do not take if allergic to any of the ingredients.

src.q: 4.3 Contraindications None known.
DO NOT take Rowatinex® if you are allergic (hypersensitive) to any of the active substances or any of the other ingredients

items.t: Not suitable in severe colic, anuria (PIL: reduced urine production) or severe urinary tract infection.

src.q: is not suitable for use in patients with severe colic, anuria or severe infection of the urinary tract
is not suitable in patients with severe pain (colic), decrease in urine production or severe infection of the urinary tract

items.t: Hydroxybenzoates in the capsule shell may cause (possibly delayed) allergic reactions.

src.q: This medicine may cause allergic reactions (possibly delayed) as it contains sodium ethyl hydroxybenzoate (E215) and sodium propyl hydroxybenzoate (E217).

items.t: Should not be used with oral anticoagulants (e.g. warfarin) or other liver-metabolised drugs where the dose is critical.

src.q: Should not be used in patients receiving oral anti-coagulants or other drugs metabolised by the liver where dose is critical.
medicines to thin your blood (oral anti-coagulants e.g. Warfarin)

items.t: Anuria: not suitable. No other renal dose guidance in the SPC.

src.q: is not suitable for use in patients with severe colic, anuria or severe infection of the urinary tract

hepatic.note: The UK SPC and PIL (MHRA products) give no hepatic impairment advice; they only warn about other liver-metabolised drugs where the dose is critical.

items.t: No teratogenic effects reported, but should not be given in the first trimester.

src.q: Although no teratogenic effects have been reported, ROWATINEX should not be given in the first trimester of pregnancy.

items.t: Should not be given to breastfeeding women (no evidence available).

src.q: Although no evidence is available, ROWATINEX should not be given to lactating females.

reproductive.note: The UK SPC and PIL (MHRA products) say nothing on fertility or contraception.

items.t: A small number of patients had slight, transient stomach upset; vomiting rarely. Side effects were uncommon and minor.

src.q: An Insignificant number of patients reported slight and transient gastric disturbance. Vomiting has been rarely reported.
side effects were uncommon and minor

items.t: Overdose: empty the stomach if recently taken; give symptomatic treatment and monitor cardiac, respiratory, renal and hepatic function.

src.q: If medication has been recently ingested, the stomach should be emptied by gastric lavage.
Monitoring of cardiac, respiratory, renal and hepatic functions are advised.

monitoring.note: The UK SPC and PIL (MHRA products) give no routine monitoring advice (only overdose monitoring).

items.t: Swallow capsules whole; do not bite or chew. Take on an empty stomach half an hour before meals.

src.q: must only be taken by swallowing the whole capsule. Do not bite or chew the capsules.
should be taken on an empty stomach half an hour before meals

items.t: Tell the doctor if taking blood thinners such as warfarin. Do not take in early pregnancy or while breastfeeding. Unlikely to affect driving.

src.q: You should not take Rowatinex® in early pregnancy (the first trimester) or if you are breast feeding.
Rowatinex® is unlikely to have any effect on your driving or ability to use machines.
